To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Harvard University is the most prolific institution, when addresses are counted whole-number; (2) Leiden University leads in the ranking, when addresses are fractional counted; (3) the most highly cited authors are involved in publishing four to five of the 305 highly-cited papers; (4) co-authorship is based on common research interests; and (5) there is a strong link between the highly-cited publications and the highly-cited researchers.

(1) Harvard University and Leiden University have published most highly-cited papers, and (2) most highly-cited scientists in LIS are active in the topics of collection and exploitation of clinical information, internet use in public communication and commercial activities, and scientometrics.

(1) the 23 highly-cited authors listed by Thomson Reuters in 2014 are also highly cited in the WoS subject category “Information science & library science,” and (2) the top-1 percent of highly-cited papers published between 2012 and 2014 in “Information Science & library Science” are related to the topics of clinical practices, public communication, and commerce on the internet, and scientometrics.
